newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines supports Peru membership in APEC.
newsitem.headline: Philippines supports Peru membership in APEC.

text.p: The Philippines supports Peru's bid to gain full membership in the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Friday.
More than 10 economies have applied to join the grouping, which plans to completely free trade and investments in the region.
"As host of the APEC summit in 1996, we would welcome Peru as a full member of APEC," Ramos told a news conference he jointly addressed with visiting Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori.
Fujimori, who arrived here on Thursday on a four-day state-visit, said Japan had also promised to support its membership bid.
APEC leaders are scheduled to decide on November 25 whether to lift a three-year moratorium on accepting new members.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, and the United States.
Ramos said he and Fujimori had agreed on the need to increase trade between the two countries, which last year stood at a mere $5 million.

"We agreed...that there is still much to be done to expand and intensify economic activities, particularly between our private sectors, in commercial activities, in scientific and technical cooperation, in culture and education, and in investments," Ramos said.
